mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at t-0w marks a broad activity contraction that suppresses discretionary trips. If that contraction persists, RETAIL_REC will fall further over the next four weeks relative to the prior four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT staying depressed or falling further.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above the prior week's level while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall, people substitute away from out-of-home shopping and dining, lowering retail-and-recreation mobility within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after a simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and decline in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in TRANSIT below its recent range signals tighter movement restrictions or fewer journeys, which should transmit quickly into fewer retail visits over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower in the following week after a week-on-week TRANSIT drop of more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM often precedes renewed neighborhood errand traffic that spills into nearby retail and recreation. If grocery mobility keeps edging up, RETAIL_REC should stabilize or improve over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its previous 28-day mean over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM continues to recover.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in PARKS and RETAIL_REC after a brief park surge indicates a broader weather-driven pullback in discretionary outings. If PARKS stays weak, retail-and-recreation mobility will also stay weak over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls back below its t-2w level after a short rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline or remain depressed within 14 days after PARKS reverses downward.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated for several weeks, home-centered routines substitute for shopping trips and entertainment outings, causing RETAIL_REC to drift down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES after a week of recovery signals renewed limits on commuting and public movement. That combination should reduce discretionary retail traffic within two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both turn down after having risen in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its previous 28-day average over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reverse downward.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w collapse in PARKS and TRANSIT indicates a broad drop in outside-the-home activity that usually spills into fewer discretionary shopping trips. If this congestion of declines persists, RETAIL_REC should be lower within one week and stay lower for the month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both fall sharply from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to drop in the next week after simultaneous sharp declines in PARKS and TRANSIT.
